P: Serve the snacks when Neo first eats the gruel on the Nebuchadnezzar.
S: Mouse swears it tastes like the real thing

Crunchy clusters of oats, puffed wheat, honey, brown butter and toasted seeds, baked golden and broken into chunks, much better than the ship's gruel. Heat the oven to 160C. Brown 60g butter in a pan until nutty, then stir in 80g honey and 40g brown sugar. Toss with 200g rolled oats, 50g puffed wheat, 60g mixed seeds and a pinch of salt. Press firmly onto a lined tray and bake 25 minutes until golden. Cool completely on the tray, then break into clusters.

I used to eat there, really good noodles

Wheat noodles tossed with spicy pork mince, sesame and chilli oil sauce, Sichuan pepper and blanched bok choy, topped with crushed peanuts and spring onion. Fry 400g pork mince in 1 tbsp oil until crisp, then add 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine. Mix 3 tbsp tahini, 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp black vinegar, 3 tbsp chilli oil, 1 tsp sugar, 1 crushed garlic clove and half a tsp ground Sichuan pepper. Cook 500g fresh wheat noodles and 4 halved baby bok choy for 2 minutes. Divide the sauce between 4 bowls, add the noodles and bok choy, top with pork, peanuts and spring onion and toss.

Two gin fizzes shaken with lemon and topped with soda: red with raspberry and cranberry, blue with blue curaçao. Everyone picks one. For 2 red drinks, shake 90ml gin, 30ml lemon juice, 30ml raspberry syrup and 60ml cranberry juice with ice and strain into 2 ice-filled glasses. For 2 blue drinks, shake 90ml gin, 30ml lemon juice, 30ml blue curaçao and 15ml sugar syrup with ice and strain into 2 ice-filled glasses. Top all 4 with 80ml soda water and add a lemon wheel.

s.note: he knows it isn't real, he eats it anyway
s.how: Cut 600g rump into cubes and season well. Sear hard in a smoking pan in batches, then toss with 40g butter and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Mix 150g sour cream with 1 tsp cracked peppercorns. Serve the bites on toothpicks with the dip.

s.note: the green code falling down the screen
s.how: Blitz a handful of parsley and dill with 2 tbsp flaky salt until green. Brush 3 lavash breads with oil, sprinkle with the herb salt and cut into long thin strips. Bake at 180C for 8 minutes until crisp.

m.note: juicy and delicious, real or not
m.how: Dry-brine 4 sirloins overnight. Sear hard, then baste with 50g butter and thyme for a minute and rest. Add 125ml red wine and 250ml stock to the pan and reduce by half, then whisk in a knob of butter. Slice the steak and pour over.

w.note: freshly baked, she knew you'd want one
w.how: Brown 150g butter and cool. Beat with 200g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g flour, half a tsp bicarb and 200g choc chips. Rest overnight. Roll into 16 balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Sprinkle with flaky salt.
